_**Agent (gpt-5.5 2026-04-25 09:03:56Z)**_

<tool-use data-tool-type="write" data-tool-name="apply_patch"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **apply_patch**</summary>
**Delete: `scripts/capture-wps-window.ps1`**

**Add: `scripts/capture-wps-window.ps1`**

```diff
+param(
+  [int]$ProcessId = 0,
+  [string]$TitleLike = "WPS",
+  [string]$OutputPath = "d:\cursor_dev\wps_ai\wps-screen.png"
+)
+
+$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
+
+Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Drawing
+Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Windows.Forms
+
+$outputDir = Split-Path -Parent $OutputPath
+if (-not [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($outputDir)) {
+  New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $outputDir -Force | Out-Null
+}
+
+$bounds = [System.Windows.Forms.SystemInformation]::VirtualScreen
+if ($bounds.Width -le 0 -or $bounds.Height -le 0) {
+  throw "Virtual screen bounds could not be resolved."
+}
+
+$bitmap = New-Object System.Drawing.Bitmap $bounds.Width, $bounds.Height
+$graphics = [System.Drawing.Graphics]::FromImage($bitmap)
+
+try {
+  $graphics.CopyFromScreen(
+    $bounds.Left,
+    $bounds.Top,
+    0,
+    0,
+    $bounds.Size,
+    [System.Drawing.CopyPixelOperation]::SourceCopy
+  )
+  $bitmap.Save($OutputPath, [System.Drawing.Imaging.ImageFormat]::Png)
+} finally {
+  $graphics.Dispose()
+  $bitmap.Dispose()
+}
+
+Write-Output $OutputPath
```

+function Invoke-RelayJson {
+  param(
+    [string]$Path,
+    [object]$Payload
+  )
+
+  $uri = "http://127.0.0.1:3888$Path"
+  $json = $Payload | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 8
+  $bytes = [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false).GetBytes($json)
+  return Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $uri -Method Post -ContentType "application/json; charset=utf-8" -Body $bytes -TimeoutSec 15
+}
+
+function Get-TestCommandStatus {
+  param([string]$CommandId)
+
+  $encodedId = [System.Uri]::EscapeDataString($CommandId)
+  $uri = "http://127.0.0.1:3888/test-command/status?id=$encodedId"
+  return Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $uri -Method Get -TimeoutSec 5
+}
+
+function Wait-TestCommandStage {
+  param(
+    [string]$CommandId,
+    [string]$Stage,
+    [int]$TimeoutSeconds = 12
+  )
+
+  $rank = @{
+    queued = 0
+    delivered = 1
+    filled = 2
+    submitted = 3
+  }
+  $targetRank = $rank[$Stage]
+  $deadline = (Get-Date).AddSeconds($TimeoutSeconds)
+  $lastStatus = $null
+
+  while ((Get-Date) -lt $deadline) {
+    $result = Get-TestCommandStatus $CommandId
+    $lastStatus = $result.status
+    $currentStage = [string]$lastStatus.stage
+
+    if ($rank.ContainsKey($currentStage) -and $rank[$currentStage] -ge $targetRank) {
+      return $lastStatus
+    }
+
+    Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 250
+  }
+
+  $lastStage = if ($lastStatus) { [string]$lastStatus.stage } else { "none" }
+  throw "Timed out waiting for test command $CommandId stage $Stage; last stage was $lastStage."
+}
+
+[WpsDesktopInput]::SetForegroundWindow($process.MainWindowHandle) | Out-Null
+Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 300
+
+if ($SubmitMode -eq "Relay") {
+  $response = Invoke-RelayJson "/test-command" ([pscustomobject]@{
+    prompt = $Prompt
+    documentTitle = $TitleLike
+    visibleDelayMs = [Math]::Max(600, $PauseAfterPasteMs)
+  })
+  $commandId = [string]$response.id
+  $filledStatus = Wait-TestCommandStage $commandId "filled" 15
+  Save-WindowScreenshot $AfterPasteScreenshotPath
+  $submittedStatus = Wait-TestCommandStage $commandId "submitted" 15
+  Save-WindowScreenshot $AfterSubmitScreenshotPath
+
+  Write-Output ("PROMPT_SENT_TO={0}" -f $process.MainWindowTitle)
+  Write-Output ("COMMAND_ID={0}" -f $commandId)
+  Write-Output ("FILLED_STAGE={0}" -f $filledStatus.stage)
+  Write-Output ("SUBMITTED_STAGE={0}" -f $submittedStatus.stage)
+  Write-Output ("SUBMIT_MODE={0}" -f $SubmitMode)
+  Write-Output ("PROMPT_CHARS={0}" -f $Prompt.Length)
+  return
+}
+
+if ($InputX -le 0 -or $InputY -le 0 -or $SendX -le 0 -or $SendY -le 0) {
+  throw "Taskpane coordinates could not be resolved."
+}
+
 [WpsDesktopInput]::SetForegroundWindow($process.MainWindowHandle) | Out-Null
 Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 300
 Set-Clipboard -Value $Prompt

+  param(
+    [string]$Path,

+
+  $uri = "http://127.0.0.1:3888$Path"
+  $json = $Payload | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 8
+  $bytes = [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false).GetBytes($json)
+  return Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $uri -Method Post -ContentType "application/json; charset=utf-8" -Body $bytes -TimeoutSec 15
+}
+
+function Get-TestCommandStatus {
+  param([string]$CommandId)
+
+  $encodedId = [System.Uri]::EscapeDataString($CommandId)
+  $uri = "http://127.0.0.1:3888/test-command/status?id=$encodedId"
+  return Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $uri -Method Get -TimeoutSec 5
+}
+
+function Wait-TestCommandStage {
+  param(
+    [string]$CommandId,
+    [string]$Stage,
+    [int]$TimeoutSeconds = 12
+  )
+
+  $rank = @{
+    queued = 0
+    delivered = 1
+    filled = 2
+    submitted = 3
+  }
+  $targetRank = $rank[$Stage]
+  $deadline = (Get-Date).AddSeconds($TimeoutSeconds)
+  $lastStatus = $null
+
+  while ((Get-Date) -lt $deadline) {
+    $result = Get-TestCommandStatus $CommandId
+    $lastStatus = $result.status
+    $currentStage = [string]$lastStatus.stage
+
+    if ($rank.ContainsKey($currentStage) -and $rank[$currentStage] -ge $targetRank) {
+      return $lastStatus
+    }
+
+    Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 250
+  }
+
+  $lastStage = if ($lastStatus) { [string]$lastStatus.stage } else { "none" }
+  throw "Timed out waiting for test command $CommandId stage $Stage; last stage was $lastStage."
+}
+

 18 │

 25 │ ```
 26 │ 
 27 │ - Run `.py`, `.js`, `.mjs`, `.bat`, or `.cmd` with their own executable, not `powershell -File`.
 28 │ - Use `rtk <program> ...` directly when PowerShell is unnecessary, for example `rtk git status`, `rtk npm test`, `rtk node script.mjs`.
 29 │ - For `.ps1` scripts that may run under Windows PowerShell 5, keep parameter defaults and control strings ASCII, or save explicitly as UTF-8 with BOM; otherwise non-ASCII defaults can be decoded incorrectly.
 30 │ - For UTF-8 prompt or fixture files that may contain Chinese, read with `.NET` encoding APIs: `[System.IO.File]::ReadAllText($path, [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false, $true))`.
 31 │ - In PowerShell functions that return objects, do not use `Write-Output` for logging; it pollutes the success pipeline. Log to a file and use `Write-Host` only for human-visible progress.

26 │ ## Rules
27 │ 
28 │ 1. Do not start with loose `click-screen` commands. Run the runner first so every step is logged.
29 │ 2. The runner shows a colored topmost status popup and writes logs under `test-artifacts\wps-ai-ui\<timestamp>\`.
30 │ 3. By default the runner closes existing WPS Writer (`wps.exe`) windows before opening a fresh document; it must not close WPS Spreadsheets (`et.exe`).

35 │ 8. Submit prompts through the local relay test command by default. The taskpane must fill the real textarea, acknowledge `filled`, wait briefly, then acknowledge `submitted` and call the normal send path.
36 │ 9. Coordinate paste/send is only a fallback diagnostic mode. Do not rely on estimated taskpane coordinates for the normal test flow.
37 │ 10. Keep the colored status popup at the top-left so it does not cover the taskpane input at the bottom.
38 │ 11. If output does not appear before timeout, stop and inspect `run.log`, `summary.json`, `prompt-filled-before-submit.png`, `prompt-submitted.png`, `captures\`, and `stuck.png`; do not repeat the same send command.
39 │ 12. Leave the generated WPS document open for manual inspection.

41 │ ## Validation Targets

45 │ - AI taskpane prompt submission.

47 │ - At least one real WPS table with expected dimensions.
48 │ - Code font and colored code characters.
49 │ - Heading-like paragraphs, bold, and italic formatting.
50 │ - Full-screen screenshots before send, after textarea fill, after submit, and after output.

 6 │ # RTK Usage
 7 │ 
 8 │ Use this skill whenever a task depends on `rtk` working correctly.
 9 │ 
10 │ ## Core Rule
11 │ 
12 │ 1. If an `rtk` command fails, do not fall back to the equivalent raw shell command.
13 │ 2. Diagnose and fix the `rtk` issue first.
14 │ 3. Only continue the main task after `rtk` is working again.
15 │ 4. Prefer RTK-native subcommands over `rtk run` / `rtk proxy` when a native subcommand exists.
16 │ 5. On Windows, quote carefully in the outer shell; many apparent RTK failures are PowerShell quoting errors.
17 │ 6. If a non-interactive command can be run through `rtk`, run it through `rtk`.
18 │ 7. Raw shell is allowed only when exact byte-for-byte output matters, the command is tiny/trivial, the command is interactive, or `rtk` would change semantics.
19 │ 8. When updating this skill, add only correct reusable RTK command forms and decision rules.
20 │ 
21 │ ## Windows Baseline Checks
22 │ 
23 │ 1. Run `rtk --version`.
24 │ 2. Run `rtk --help`.
25 │ 3. Run `rtk gain`.
26 │ 4. Run `rtk init -g --show` for Claude hook status.
27 │ 5. Run `rtk init -g --codex --show` for Codex global status.
28 │ 6. Run `rtk verify`.
29 │ 7. Run `rtk proxy where.exe rtk` to confirm the active binary.
30 │ 8. On Windows release installs, prefer the official GitHub asset `rtk-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip`.
31 │ 
32 │ Known-good Windows baseline observed for `rtk 0.37.2`:
33 │ 
34 │ ```bash
35 │ rtk --version
36 │ rtk --help
37 │ rtk gain
38 │ rtk verify
39 │ rtk init -g --show
40 │ rtk init -g --codex --show
41 │ rtk proxy where.exe rtk
42 │ ```
43 │

51 │ rtk rewrite "git status --short"
52 │ rtk proxy git status --short

55 │ rtk run "git branch --show-current"

+function Save-WithCopyFromScreen {
+  param(
+    [System.Drawing.Rectangle]$Bounds,
+    [string]$Path
+  )
+
+  $bitmap = New-Object System.Drawing.Bitmap $Bounds.Width, $Bounds.Height
+  $graphics = [System.Drawing.Graphics]::FromImage($bitmap)
+
+  try {
+    $graphics.CopyFromScreen(
+      $Bounds.Left,
+      $Bounds.Top,
+      0,
+      0,
+      $Bounds.Size,
+      [System.Drawing.CopyPixelOperation]::SourceCopy
+    )
+    $bitmap.Save($Path, [System.Drawing.Imaging.ImageFormat]::Png)
+  } finally {
+    $graphics.Dispose()
+    $bitmap.Dispose()
+  }
+}
+
+function Save-WithBitBlt {
+  param(
+    [System.Drawing.Rectangle]$Bounds,
+    [string]$Path
+  )
+
+  $bitmap = New-Object System.Drawing.Bitmap $Bounds.Width, $Bounds.Height
+  $graphics = [System.Drawing.Graphics]::FromImage($bitmap)
+  $destDc = $graphics.GetHdc()
+  $screenDc = [ScreenCaptureNative]::GetDC([IntPtr]::Zero)
+  $SRCCOPY = 0x00CC0020
+
+  try {
+    if ($screenDc -eq [IntPtr]::Zero) {
+      throw "Could not acquire desktop DC."
+    }
+
+    $ok = [ScreenCaptureNative]::BitBlt(
+      $destDc,
+      0,
+      0,
+      $Bounds.Width,
+      $Bounds.Height,
+      $screenDc,
+      $Bounds.Left,
+      $Bounds.Top,
+      $SRCCOPY
+    )
+
+    if (-not $ok) {
+      throw "Desktop BitBlt failed."
+    }
+
+    $bitmap.Save($Path, [System.Drawing.Imaging.ImageFormat]::Png)
+  } finally {
+    if ($screenDc -ne [IntPtr]::Zero) {
+      [ScreenCaptureNative]::ReleaseDC([IntPtr]::Zero, $screenDc) | Out-Null
+    }
+    $graphics.ReleaseHdc($destDc)
+    $graphics.Dispose()
+    $bitmap.Dispose()
+  }
+}
+
+$lastError = $null
+for ($attempt = 1; $attempt -le 3; $attempt++) {
+  try {
+    Save-WithCopyFromScreen $bounds $OutputPath
+    Write-Output $OutputPath
+    exit 0
+  } catch {
+    $lastError = $_.Exception.Message
+    Start-Sleep -Milliseconds (150 * $attempt)
+  }
+}
+
+try {
+  Save-WithBitBlt $bounds $OutputPath
+} catch {
+  throw "Full-screen capture failed. CopyFromScreen: $lastError; BitBlt: $($_.Exception.Message)"

 Write-Output $OutputPath

# RTK - Rust Token Killer (Codex CLI)

**Usage**: Token-optimized CLI proxy for shell commands.

## Rule

Always prefix shell commands with `rtk`.

Examples:

```bash
rtk git status
rtk cargo test
rtk npm run build
rtk pytest -q
```

## Meta Commands

```bash
rtk gain            # Token savings analytics
rtk gain --history  # Recent command savings history
rtk proxy <cmd>     # Run raw command without filtering
```

## Verification

```bash
rtk --version
rtk gain
which rtk
```

# RTK Usage

Use this skill whenever a task depends on `rtk` working correctly.

## Core Rule

1. If an `rtk` command fails, do not fall back to the equivalent raw shell command.
2. Diagnose and fix the `rtk` issue first.
3. Only continue the main task after `rtk` is working again.
4. Prefer RTK-native subcommands over `rtk run` / `rtk proxy` when a native subcommand exists.
5. On Windows, quote carefully in the outer shell; many apparent RTK failures are PowerShell quoting errors.
6. If a non-interactive command can be run through `rtk`, run it through `rtk`.
7. Raw shell is allowed only when exact byte-for-byte output matters, the command is tiny/trivial, the command is interactive, or `rtk` would change semantics.
8. When updating this skill, add only correct reusable RTK command forms and decision rules.

## Windows Baseline Checks

1. Run `rtk --version`.
2. Run `rtk --help`.
3. Run `rtk gain`.
4. Run `rtk init -g --show` for Claude hook status.
5. Run `rtk init -g --codex --show` for Codex global status.
6. Run `rtk verify`.
7. Run `rtk proxy where.exe rtk` to confirm the active binary.
8. On Windows release installs, prefer the official GitHub asset `rtk-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip`.

Known-good Windows baseline observed for `rtk 0.37.2`:

```bash
rtk --version
rtk --help
rtk gain
rtk verify
rtk init -g --show
rtk init -g --codex --show
rtk proxy where.exe rtk
```

## Correct Command Patterns

Use these forms exactly:

```bash
rtk env --filter PATH
rtk json package.json
rtk rewrite "git status --short"
rtk proxy git status --short
rtk proxy powershell -NoProfile -Command "Get-Content package.json -TotalCount 20"
rtk powershell -NoProfile -Command "Get-Content package.json -TotalCount 20"
rtk run "git branch --show-current"
rtk run -c "git status --short"
rtk verify
rtk help hook
rtk hook check git status --short
```

Rules:

1. `rtk env` uses `--filter`; do not pass variable names as positional arguments.
2. `rtk json` takes a JSON file path; do not pass inline JSON text.
3. `rtk rewrite` can exit non-zero even after printing a valid rewrite in some Windows builds; judge by printed output and `rtk rewrite --help`, not by code alone.
4. `rtk proxy` is acceptable for diagnosis because it still goes through `rtk`.
5. `rtk run` uses shell execution semantics; prefer RTK-native commands first, then `rtk proxy` when quoting is simpler.
6. Do not use `rtk read --line` or `--line-count`; current `rtk read` supports `--max-lines`, `--tail-lines`, and `--line-numbers`.
7. `rtk powershell ...` is valid when PowerShell is the intended program; `rtk proxy powershell ...` is also acceptable for diagnosis.
8. On this Windows environment, use `powershell`, not `pwsh`, unless `rtk proxy where.exe pwsh` confirms PowerShell 7 is installed.

## Correct Windows Recipes

Use these positive patterns for recurring Windows command scenarios:

1. PowerShell on this machine: use `rtk powershell ...` by default; only use `pwsh` after `rtk proxy where.exe pwsh` confirms it exists.
2. Inline PowerShell containing `$`, `$env:...`, or `$_`: use outer single quotes around the PowerShell script, or escape each `$` as `` `$ `` when outer double quotes are unavoidable.
3. PowerShell regex alternation: quote the regex inside the PowerShell script, for example `-match "node|vite|wps"`.
4. Python scripts: run with `rtk python script.py`; do not use PowerShell as the interpreter.
5. Node scripts: run with `rtk node script.mjs` or the project package wrapper, not through PowerShell unless shell features are needed.
6. PowerShell scripts: run with `rtk powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\script.ps1`.
7. Builds with post-build installers: use the project wrapper through `rtk`, then verify generated artifact timestamps and install directories if the command takes longer than expected.
8. Command diagnosis: classify failures as RTK resolution, PowerShell parsing, target-program error, or timeout before retrying.

## High-Frequency Command Recipes

Use this section before inventing command syntax.

### Git

Prefer RTK-native Git wrappers:

```bash
rtk git status --short
rtk git diff --stat
rtk git diff -- path/to/file
rtk proxy git diff -- path/to/file path/to/other-file
rtk git log -1 --oneline
rtk git add path/to/file
rtk git commit -m "Message"
rtk git push origin main
rtk git pull
rtk git branch --show-current
```

Notes:

1. `rtk git add`, `rtk git commit`, and `rtk git push` intentionally produce compact `ok` output.
2. Use `rtk proxy git ...` only when exact raw Git output is needed.

# Windows PowerShell

Use this skill before running non-trivial PowerShell commands on Windows. Keep updates concise: add only correct reusable command forms and decision rules, not failing commands or incident notes.

## Command Review

Before executing, check:

- Entry mode: `rtk powershell -Command` for inline script, `rtk powershell -File` only for `.ps1`.
- Write scope: target files, install directories, generated artifacts, processes.
- Fragile tokens: `$_`, `$env:...`, `|`, `>`, `<`, `&`, `;`, quotes, paths with spaces.
- Whether a small read-only probe should run before a write/copy/remove/build/install command.

## Entry Rules

- Run PowerShell scripts as:

```powershell
rtk powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ".\scripts\task.ps1"
```

- Run `.py`, `.js`, `.mjs`, `.bat`, or `.cmd` with their own executable, not `powershell -File`.
- Use `rtk <program> ...` directly when PowerShell is unnecessary, for example `rtk git status`, `rtk npm test`, `rtk node script.mjs`.
- For `.ps1` scripts that may run under Windows PowerShell 5, keep parameter defaults and control strings ASCII, or save explicitly as UTF-8 with BOM; otherwise non-ASCII defaults can be decoded incorrectly.
- For UTF-8 prompt or fixture files that may contain Chinese, read with `.NET` encoding APIs: `[System.IO.File]::ReadAllText($path, [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false, $true))`.
- In PowerShell functions that return objects, do not use `Write-Output` for logging; it pollutes the success pipeline. Log to a file and use `Write-Host` only for human-visible progress.

## Quoting Rules

Prefer outer single quotes when inline PowerShell contains `$`, `$env:...`, or `$_`:

```powershell
rtk powershell -NoProfile -Command 'Get-Process | Where-Object { $_.ProcessName -match "node|vite|wps" } | Select-Object Id,ProcessName'
```

```powershell
rtk powershell -NoProfile -Command '$p = Join-Path $env:APPDATA "kingsoft\wps"; Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $p'
```

When outer double quotes are required by the caller, escape every PowerShell `$` as backtick-dollar:

```powershell
rtk powershell -NoProfile -Command "`$target = Join-Path `$env:APPDATA 'kingsoft\wps\jsaddons'; Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath `$target -Directory | Select-Object Name,LastWriteTime"
```

For `$_` with outer double quotes, escape `$_` and quote regex alternation inside the script:

```powershell
rtk powershell -NoProfile -Command "Get-Process | Where-Object { `$_.ProcessName -match 'node|vite|wps|powershell' } | Select-Object Id,ProcessName,StartTime"
```

For nested quotes in WMI/CIM filters, assign the filter to a variable first:

```powershell
rtk powershell -NoProfile -Command "`$filter = 'Name = ''powershell.exe'''; Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter `$filter | Select-Object ProcessId,CommandLine"
```

## Paths And Files

- Use `-LiteralPath` for exact paths, especially paths with spaces, brackets, wildcards, or non-ASCII characters.
- Quote all Windows paths.
- Prefer `Join-Path` for paths built from `$env:APPDATA`, `$HOME`, or workspace variables.

Read a file:

```powershell
rtk powershell -NoProfile -Command 'Get-Content -LiteralPath "C:\path\file.txt"'
```

List selected files:

```powershell
rtk powershell -NoProfile -Command 'Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath "C:\path" -Force | Select-Object Name,LastWriteTime,Length'
```

Inspect generated or installed artifacts under `%APPDATA%`:

```powershell
rtk powershell -NoProfile -Command "`$asset = Join-Path `$env:APPDATA 'kingsoft\wps\jsaddons\wps-ai_1.0.4\assets'; Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath `$asset -Filter 'taskpane-*.js' | Select-Object Name,LastWriteTime,Length"
```

For timestamp checks where the target directory is already specific, list and sort the target directly instead of embedding complex regex filters:

```powershell
rtk powershell -NoProfile -Command '$target = Join-Path $env:APPDATA "kingsoft\wps\jsaddons\wps-ai_1.0.4"; Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $target -Recurse -File | Sort-Object LastWriteTime -Descending | Select-Object -First 12 FullName,LastWriteTime,Length'
```

For WPS-AI-CHAT desktop UI tests, use the project runner instead of loose click commands:

```powershell
rtk powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ".\scripts\run-wps-ai-ui-test.ps1"
```

WPS-AI-CHAT test runner rules:

- The runner closes existing WPS Writer (`wps.exe`) windows by default and must not close WPS Spreadsheets (`et.exe`).
- Use recursive UI Automation traversal for nested WPS/CEF panes; detect either `CefBrowserWindow` or `KxJSCTPWidget`.
- Keep periodic full-screen screenshots under the run directory `
... (truncated)

# WPS AI Testing

Use the project test runner instead of ad hoc click commands.

## Entry Point

From `d:\cursor_dev\wps_ai`:

```powershell
rtk powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ".\scripts\run-wps-ai-ui-test.ps1"
```

Options:

```powershell
rtk powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ".\scripts\run-wps-ai-ui-test.ps1" -WaitSeconds 240
rtk powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ".\scripts\run-wps-ai-ui-test.ps1" -NoPopup
rtk powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ".\scripts\run-wps-ai-ui-test.ps1" -KeepExistingWps
```

## Rules

1. Do not start with loose `click-screen` commands. Run the runner first so every step is logged.
2. The runner shows a colored topmost status popup and writes logs under `test-artifacts\wps-ai-ui\<timestamp>\`.
3. By default the runner closes existing WPS Writer (`wps.exe`) windows before opening a fresh document; it must not close WPS Spreadsheets (`et.exe`).
4. The runner writes periodic full-screen screenshots under `captures\` while waiting for the taskpane and document output.
5. Save each test document as a unique ASCII `.docx` in the run folder before sending the prompt; this avoids stale `鏂囧瓧鏂囩1` conversation history.
6. The fixed prompt is `scripts\wps-ai-render-test-prompt.txt`; read prompt files with .NET UTF-8 APIs, not plain `Get-Content`, when clipboard text may contain Chinese.
7. Use recursive UI Automation traversal to find `CefBrowserWindow` or `KxJSCTPWidget`; single-call `FindFirst` can miss nested WPS/CEF panes.
8. Submit prompts through the local relay test command by default. The taskpane must fill the real textarea, acknowledge `filled`, wait briefly, then acknowledge `submitted` and call the normal send path.
9. Coordinate paste/send is only a fallback diagnostic mode. Do not rely on estimated taskpane coordinates for the normal test flow.
10. Keep the colored status popup at the top-left so it does not cover the taskpane input at the bottom.
11. If output does not appear before timeout, stop and inspect `run.log`, `summary.json`, `prompt-filled-before-submit.png`, `prompt-submitted.png`, `captures\`, and `stuck.png`; do not repeat the same send command.
12. Leave the generated WPS document open for manual inspection.

## Validation Targets

The test must check:

- AI taskpane prompt submission.
- WPS body text output length.
- At least one real WPS table with expected dimensions.
- Code font and colored code characters.
- Heading-like paragraphs, bold, and italic formatting.
- Full-screen screenshots before send, after textarea fill, after submit, and after output.
```

function activeCodeBlockContext(state) {
  return findLastContext(
    state,
    (entry) => entry.type === CODE_BLOCK || entry.type === CODE_FENCE
  );
}

function applyTextStyle(range, style) {
  const font = range.Font;

  font.Bold = style.bold ? 1 : 0;
  font.Italic = style.italic ? 1 : 0;

  if (style.size) {
    font.Size = style.size;
  }

  if (style.code) {
    font.Name = "Consolas";
    font.NameAscii = "Consolas";
  }

  if (style.color !== null && style.color !== undefined) {
    try {
      font.Color = style.color;
    } catch {
      // Some hosts may not expose font color.
    }
  }

  try {
    font.StrikeThrough = style.strike ? 1 : 0;
  } catch {
    // Some hosts may not expose StrikeThrough.
  }

  try {
    range.Underline = style.underline ? 1 : 0;
  } catch {
    // Some hosts may not expose Underline on range.
  }
}

function captureBaseStyle(range) {
  const font = range.Font;
  const size = Number(font.Size);

  return {
    name: String(font.Name ?? ""),
    nameAscii: String(font.NameAscii ?? font.Name ?? ""),
    size: Number.isFinite(size) ? size : null
  };
}

function createPaperBodyStyle() {
  return { ...PAPER_BODY_STYLE };
}

 For nested quotes in WMI/CIM filters, assign the filter to a variable first:
 
 ```powershell
 rtk powershell -NoProfile -Command "`$filter = 'Name = ''powershell.exe'''; Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter `$filter | Select-Object ProcessId,CommandLine"
 ```
+
+Do not use backslash to escape quotes for PowerShell. When a `-Command` script needs paths with spaces, use single quotes inside the script:
+
+```powershell
+rtk powershell -NoProfile -Command "Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath 'D:\Programs\WPS AI Sessions' -Filter 'WpsAiUiTest*.md'"
+```
@@
 Read a file:
 
 ```powershell
 rtk powershell -NoProfile -Command 'Get-Content -LiteralPath "C:\path\file.txt"'
 ```
+
+For ordinary file reads, especially with paths containing spaces, prefer `rtk read` and quote the full path:
+
+```powershell
+rtk read -n --max-lines 120 'D:\Programs\WPS AI Sessions\session.md'
+```

function applyCodeFormat(range) {
  const font = range.Font;

function applyCodeBlockBorder(range) {
  const borderColor = cssColorToWpsColor(CODE_BLOCK_BORDER_COLOR);

  try {
    range.Borders.Enable = 1;
  } catch {
    // Some hosts may not expose paragraph borders.

  try {
    range.Borders.OutsideLineStyle = 1;
    range.Borders.OutsideColor = borderColor;

    // Some hosts may not expose outside border shortcuts.

      // Internal borders are optional for paragraph groups.

function formatCurlFailure(stderr) {
  const message = stderr.trim();
  if (!message) {
    return "Failed to reach NVIDIA upstream";
  }

  return message.replace(/^curl:\s*/i, "");
}

function normalizeContent(content) {
  if (typeof content === "string") {
    return content;
  }

  if (!Array.isArray(content)) {
    return "";
  }

  return content
    .map((item) => {
      if (typeof item === "string") {
        return item;
      }

      if (item && typeof item === "object" && "text" in item) {
        return String(item.text ?? "");
      }

      return "";
    })
    .join("");
}

function extractChunk(payload) {
  const choice = payload?.choices?.[0];
  if (!choice) {
    return "";
  }

  return (
    normalizeContent(choice.delta?.content) ||
    normalizeContent(choice.message?.content) ||
    ""
  );
}

function parseSseEvent(block) {
  const data = block
    .split(/\r?\n/)
    .filter((line) => line.startsWith("data:"))
    .map((line) => line.slice(5).trim())
    .join("\n")
    .trim();

  if (!data || data === "[DONE]") {
    return null;
  }

  try {
    return JSON.parse(data);
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}

function createCurlArgs({
  authorization,
  url,
  method = "GET",
  headers = [],
  dataFromStdin = false,
  stream = false
}) {
  const args = ["-sS"];

  if (stream) {
    args.push("-N");
  }

  args.push("-f", "-X", method);

  if (authorization) {
    args.push("-H", `Authorization: ${authorization}`);
  }

  for (const header of headers) {
    args.push("-H", header);
  }

  if (dataFromStdin) {
    args.push("--data-binary", "@-");
  }

  args.push(url);
  return args;
}

function runCurlBuffered({
  authorization,
  url,
  method = "GET",
  headers = [],
  body = ""
}) {
  const attempts = hasProxyConfigured(PROXY_ENV)
    ? [
        { env: PROXY_ENV, label: "proxy" },
        { env: DIRECT_ENV, label: "direct" }
      ]
    : [{ env: PROXY_ENV, label: "direct" }];

  function runAttempt(index) {
    return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
      const attempt = attempts[index];
      const curl = spawn(
        CURL_BIN,
        createCurlArgs({
          authorization,
          url,
          method,
          headers,
          dataFromStdin: method !== "GET"
        }),
        {
          env: attempt.env,
          stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "pipe"],
          windowsHide: true
        }
      );

      let stdout = "";
      let stderr = "";

      curl.on("error", (error) => {
        reject(error instanceof Error ? error : new Error("Failed to start curl"));
      });

      curl.stdout.on("data", (chunk) => {
        stdout += chunk.toString("utf8");
      });

      curl.stderr.on("data", (chunk) => {
        stderr += chunk.toString("utf8");
      });

function documentMatchesTestCommand(command, document) {
  const target = String(command.documentTitle || command.documentKey || "").trim().toLowerCase();
  if (!target) {
    return true;
  }

  const normalized = normalizeTestDocument(document);
  if (!normalized) {
    return false;
  }

  return [normalized.key, normalized.title, normalized.name, normalized.fullName]
    .filter(Boolean)
    .some((value) => value.toLowerCase().includes(target));
}

async function handleTestCommandPush(req, res) {
  let body;
  try {
    body = await readJsonBody(req);
  } catch {
    sendJson(res, 400, {
      error: {
        message: "Invalid JSON body"
      }
    });
    return;
  }

  const prompt = String(body?.prompt ?? "");
  if (!prompt.trim()) {
    sendJson(res, 400, {
      error: {
        message: "Prompt is required"
      }
    });
    return;
  }

  const id = `test-${Date.now()}-${++testCommandSeq}`;
  pendingTestCommand = {
    id,
    prompt,
    documentTitle: String(body?.documentTitle ?? ""),
    documentKey: String(body?.documentKey ?? ""),
    visibleDelayMs: Math.min(8000, Math.max(600, Number(body?.visibleDelayMs) || 1800)),
    createdAt: new Date().toISOString()
  };

  rememberTestCommandStatus(id, {
    stage: "queued",
    command: {
      id,
      documentTitle: pendingTestCommand.documentTitle,
      documentKey: pendingTestCommand.documentKey,
      promptLength: prompt.length,
      visibleDelayMs: pendingTestCommand.visibleDelayMs
    }
  });

  sendJson(res, 200, {
    ok: true,
    id,
    stage: "queued"
  });
}

async function handleTestCommandPoll(req, res) {
  let body;
  try {
    body = await readJsonBody(req);
  } catch {
    sendJson(res, 400, {
      error: {
        message: "Invalid JSON body"
      }
    });
    return;
  }

  if (!pendingTestCommand) {
    sendJson(res, 200, {
      ok: true,
      command: null
    });
    return;
  }

  if (!documentMatchesTestCommand(pendingTestCommand, body?.document)) {
    sendJson(res, 200, {
      ok: true,
      command: null
    });
    return;
  }

  const command = pendingTestCommand;
  pendingTestCommand = null;
  rememberTestCommandStatus(command.id, {
    stage: "delivered",
    document: normalizeTestDocument(body?.document)
  });

  sendJson(res, 200, {
    ok: true,
    command
  });
}

async function handleTestCommandAck(req, res) {
  let body;
  try {
    body = await readJsonBody(req);
  } catch {
    sendJson(res, 400, {
      error: {
        message: "Invalid JSON body"
      }
    });
    return;
  }

  const id = String(body?.id ?? "");
  if (!id) {
    sendJson(res, 400, {
      error: {
        message: "Command id is required"
      }
    });
    return;
  }

  const status = rememberTestCommandStatus(id, {
    stage: String(body?.stage ?? "ack"),
    document: normalizeTestDocument(body?.document),
    detail: body?.detail || {}
  });

  sendJson(res, 200, {
    ok: true,
    status
  });
}

function handleTestCommandStatus(res, requestUrl) {
  const id = String(requestUrl.searchParams.get("id") ?? "");
  if (!id) {
    sendJson(res, 400, {
      error: {
        message: "Command id is required"
      }
    });
    return;
  }

  sendJson(res, 200, {
    ok: true,
    status: testCommandStatuses.get(id) || null
  });
}

# RTK Usage

Use this skill whenever a task depends on `rtk` working correctly.

## Core Rule

1. If an `rtk` command fails, do not fall back to the equivalent raw shell command.
2. Diagnose and fix the `rtk` issue first.
3. Only continue the main task after `rtk` is working again.
4. Prefer RTK-native subcommands over `rtk run` / `rtk proxy` when a native subcommand exists.
5. On Windows, quote carefully in the outer shell; many apparent RTK failures are PowerShell quoting errors.
6. If a non-interactive command can be run through `rtk`, run it through `rtk`.
7. Raw shell is allowed only when exact byte-for-byte output matters, the command is tiny/trivial, the command is interactive, or `rtk` would change semantics.
8. When updating this skill, add only correct reusable RTK command forms and decision rules.

## Windows Baseline Checks

1. Run `rtk --version`.
2. Run `rtk --help`.
3. Run `rtk gain`.
4. Run `rtk init -g --show` for Claude hook status.
5. Run `rtk init -g --codex --show` for Codex global status.
6. Run `rtk verify`.
7. Run `rtk proxy where.exe rtk` to confirm the active binary.
8. On Windows release installs, prefer the official GitHub asset `rtk-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip`.

Known-good Windows baseline observed for `rtk 0.37.2`:

```bash
rtk --version
rtk --help
rtk gain
rtk verify
rtk init -g --show
rtk init -g --codex --show
rtk proxy where.exe rtk
```

## Correct Command Patterns

Use these forms exactly:

```bash
rtk env --filter PATH
rtk json package.json
rtk rewrite "git status --short"
rtk proxy git status --short
rtk proxy powershell -NoProfile -Command "Get-Content package.json -TotalCount 20"
rtk powershell -NoProfile -Command "Get-Content package.json -TotalCount 20"
rtk run "git branch --show-current"
rtk run -c "git status --short"
rtk verify
rtk help hook
rtk hook check git status --short
```

Rules:

1. `rtk env` uses `--filter`; do not pass variable names as positional arguments.
2. `rtk json` takes a JSON file path; do not pass inline JSON text.
3. `rtk rewrite` can exit non-zero even after printing a valid rewrite in some Windows builds; judge by printed output and `rtk rewrite --help`, not by code alone.
4. `rtk proxy` is acceptable for diagnosis because it still goes through `rtk`.
5. `rtk run` uses shell execution semantics; prefer RTK-native commands first, then `rtk proxy` when quoting is simpler.
6. Do not use `rtk read --line` or `--line-count`; current `rtk read` supports `--max-lines`, `--tail-lines`, and `--line-numbers`.
7. `rtk powershell ...` is valid when PowerShell is the intended program; `rtk proxy powershell ...` is also acceptable for diagnosis.
8. On this Windows environment, use `powershell`, not `pwsh`, unless `rtk proxy where.exe pwsh` confirms PowerShell 7 is installed.

## Correct Windows Recipes

Use these positive patterns for recurring Windows command scenarios:

1. PowerShell on this machine: use `rtk powershell ...` by default; only use `pwsh` after `rtk proxy where.exe pwsh` confirms it exists.
2. Inline PowerShell containing `$`, `$env:...`, or `$_`: use outer single quotes around the PowerShell script, or escape each `$` as `` `$ `` when outer double quotes are unavoidable.
3. PowerShell regex alternation: quote the regex inside the PowerShell script, for example `-match "node|vite|wps"`.
4. Python scripts: run with `rtk python script.py`; do not use PowerShell as the interpreter.
5. Node scripts: run with `rtk node script.mjs` or the project package wrapper, not through PowerShell unless shell features are needed.
6. PowerShell scripts: run with `rtk powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\script.ps1`.
7. Builds with post-build installers: use the project wrapper through `rtk`, then verify generated artifact timestamps and install directories if the command takes longer than expected.
8. Command diagnosis: classify failures as RTK resolution, PowerShell parsing, target-program error, or timeout before retrying.

## High-Frequency Command Recipes

Use this section before inventing command syntax.

### Git

Prefer RTK-native Git wrappers:

```bash
rtk git status --short
rtk git diff --stat
rtk git diff -- path/to/file
rtk proxy git diff -- path/to/file path/to/other-file
rtk git log -1 --oneline
rtk git add path/to/file
rtk git commit -m "Message"
rtk git push origin main
rtk git pull
rtk git branch --show-current
```

Notes:

1. `rtk git add`, `rtk git commit`, and `rtk git push` intentionally produce compact `ok` output.
2. Use `rtk proxy git ...` only when exact raw Git output is needed.

# Windows PowerShell

Use this skill before running non-trivial PowerShell commands on Windows. Keep updates concise: add only correct reusable command forms and decision rules, not failing commands or incident notes.

## Command Review

Before executing, check:

- Entry mode: `rtk powershell -Command` for inline script, `rtk powershell -File` only for `.ps1`.
- Write scope: target files, install directories, generated artifacts, processes.
- Fragile tokens: `$_`, `$env:...`, `|`, `>`, `<`, `&`, `;`, quotes, paths with spaces.
- Whether a small read-only probe should run before a write/copy/remove/build/install command.

## Entry Rules

- Run PowerShell scripts as:

```powershell
rtk powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ".\scripts\task.ps1"
```

- Run `.py`, `.js`, `.mjs`, `.bat`, or `.cmd` with their own executable, not `powershell -File`.
- Use `rtk <program> ...` directly when PowerShell is unnecessary, for example `rtk git status`, `rtk npm test`, `rtk node script.mjs`.
- For `.ps1` scripts that may run under Windows PowerShell 5, keep parameter defaults and control strings ASCII, or save explicitly as UTF-8 with BOM; otherwise non-ASCII defaults can be decoded incorrectly.
- For UTF-8 prompt or fixture files that may contain Chinese, read with `.NET` encoding APIs: `[System.IO.File]::ReadAllText($path, [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false, $true))`.
- In PowerShell functions that return objects, do not use `Write-Output` for logging; it pollutes the success pipeline. Log to a file and use `Write-Host` only for human-visible progress.

## Quoting Rules

Prefer outer single quotes when inline PowerShell contains `$`, `$env:...`, or `$_`:

```powershell
rtk powershell -NoProfile -Command 'Get-Process | Where-Object { $_.ProcessName -match "node|vite|wps" } | Select-Object Id,ProcessName'
```

```powershell
rtk powershell -NoProfile -Command '$p = Join-Path $env:APPDATA "kingsoft\wps"; Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $p'
```

When outer double quotes are required by the caller, escape every PowerShell `$` as backtick-dollar:

```powershell
rtk powershell -NoProfile -Command "`$target = Join-Path `$env:APPDATA 'kingsoft\wps\jsaddons'; Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath `$target -Directory | Select-Object Name,LastWriteTime"
```

For `$_` with outer double quotes, escape `$_` and quote regex alternation inside the script:

```powershell
rtk powershell -NoProfile -Command "Get-Process | Where-Object { `$_.ProcessName -match 'node|vite|wps|powershell' } | Select-Object Id,ProcessName,StartTime"
```

For nested quotes in WMI/CIM filters, assign the filter to a variable first:

```powershell
rtk powershell -NoProfile -Command "`$filter = 'Name = ''powershell.exe'''; Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter `$filter | Select-Object ProcessId,CommandLine"
```

Do not use backslash to escape quotes for PowerShell. When a `-Command` script needs paths with spaces, use single quotes inside the script:

```powershell
rtk powershell -NoProfile -Command "Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath 'D:\Programs\WPS AI Sessions' -Filter 'WpsAiUiTest*.md'"
```

## Paths And Files

- Use `-LiteralPath` for exact paths, especially paths with spaces, brackets, wildcards, or non-ASCII characters.
- Quote all Windows paths.
- Prefer `Join-Path` for paths built from `$env:APPDATA`, `$HOME`, or workspace variables.

Read a file:

```powershell
rtk powershell -NoProfile -Command 'Get-Content -LiteralPath "C:\path\file.txt"'
```

For ordinary file reads, especially with paths containing spaces, prefer `rtk read` and quote the full path:

```powershell
rtk read -n --max-lines 120 'D:\Programs\WPS AI Sessions\session.md'
```

List selected files:

```powershell
rtk powershell -NoProfile -Command 'Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath "C:\path" -Force | Select-Object Name,LastWriteTime,Length'
```

Inspect generated or installed artifacts under `%APPDATA%`:

```powershell
rtk powershell -NoProfile -Command "`$asset = Join-Path `$env:APPDATA 'kingsoft\wps\jsaddons\wps-ai_1.0.4\assets'; Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath `$asset -Filter 'taskpane-*.js' | Select-Object Name,LastWriteTime,Length"
```

For timestamp checks where the target directory is already specific, list and sort the target directly instead of embedding complex regex filters:

```powershell
rtk powershell -NoProfile -Command '$target = Join-Path $env:APPDATA "kingsoft\wps\jsaddons\wps-ai_1.0.4"; Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $target -Recurse -File | Sort-Object LastWriteTime -Descending | Select-Object -First 12 FullName,LastWriteTime,Length'
```

# WPS AI Testing

Use the project test runner instead of ad hoc click commands.

## Entry Point

From `d:\cursor_dev\wps_ai`:

```powershell
rtk powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ".\scripts\run-wps-ai-ui-test.ps1"
```

Options:

```powershell
rtk powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ".\scripts\run-wps-ai-ui-test.ps1" -WaitSeconds 240
rtk powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ".\scripts\run-wps-ai-ui-test.ps1" -NoPopup
rtk powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ".\scripts\run-wps-ai-ui-test.ps1" -KeepExistingWps
```

## Rules

1. Do not start with loose `click-screen` commands. Run the runner first so every step is logged.
2. The runner shows a colored topmost status popup and writes logs under `test-artifacts\wps-ai-ui\<timestamp>\`.
3. By default the runner closes existing WPS Writer (`wps.exe`) windows before opening a fresh document; it must not close WPS Spreadsheets (`et.exe`).
4. The runner writes periodic full-screen screenshots under `captures\` while waiting for the taskpane and document output.
5. Save each test document as a unique ASCII `.docx` in the run folder before sending the prompt; this avoids stale `文字文稿1` conversation history.
6. The fixed prompt is `scripts\wps-ai-render-test-prompt.txt`; read prompt files with .NET UTF-8 APIs, not plain `Get-Content`, when clipboard text may contain Chinese.
7. Use recursive UI Automation traversal to find `CefBrowserWindow` or `KxJSCTPWidget`; single-call `FindFirst` can miss nested WPS/CEF panes.
8. Submit prompts through the local relay test command by default. The taskpane must fill the real textarea, acknowledge `filled`, wait briefly, then acknowledge `submitted` and call the normal send path.
9. Coordinate paste/send is only a fallback diagnostic mode. Do not rely on estimated taskpane coordinates for the normal test flow.
10. Keep the colored status popup at the top-left so it does not cover the taskpane input at the bottom.
11. If output does not appear before timeout, stop and inspect `run.log`, `summary.json`, `prompt-filled-before-submit.png`, `prompt-submitted.png`, `captures\`, and `stuck.png`; do not repeat the same send command.
12. Leave the generated WPS document open for manual inspection.

## Validation Targets

The test must check:

- AI taskpane prompt submission.
- WPS body text output length.
- At least one real WPS table with expected dimensions.
- Code font and colored code characters.
- Heading-like paragraphs, bold, and italic formatting.
- Full-screen screenshots before send, after textarea fill, after submit, and after output.

+param(

+function Normalize-Text {

+
+  $value = [string]($Text ?? "")
+  $value = $value -replace "[\u0000-\u001f]", " "
+  $value = $value -replace "\s+", " "
+  return $value.Trim()
+}
+
+function Read-StyleName {

+
+  try {
+    return [string]$Range.Style.NameLocal
+  } catch {
+    try {
+      return [string]$Range.Style
+    } catch {
+      return ""

+  }

+function Read-ParagraphRecord {

+    [int]$Index
+  )
+
+  $range = $Paragraph.Range
+  $text = Normalize-Text $range.Text
+  if ($text.Length -gt 140) {

+  $styleName = Read-StyleName $range
+  $outline = $null

+

+  try { $fontName = [string]$range.Font.Name } catch {}
+  try { $fontNameAscii = [string]$range.Font.NameAscii } catch {}
+  try { $fontSize = [double]$range.Font.Size } catch {}
+  try { $bold = [int]$range.Font.Bold } catch {}
+  try { $italic = [int]$range.Font.Italic } catch {}
+  try { $color = [int]$range.Font.Color } catch {}
+  try { $shading = [int]$range.Shading.BackgroundPatternColor } catch {}
+  try { $alignment = [string]$range.ParagraphFormat.Alignment } catch {}
+  try { $leftIndent = [double]$range.ParagraphFormat.CharacterUnitLeftIndent } catch {}
+  try { $firstIndent = [double]$range.ParagraphFormat.CharacterUnitFirstLineIndent } catch {}
+  try { $lineSpacing = [double]$range.ParagraphFormat.LineSpacing } catch {}
+  try { $spaceBefore = [double]$range.ParagraphFormat.SpaceBefore } catch {}
+  try { $spaceAfter = [double]$range.ParagraphFormat.SpaceAfter } catch {}
+
+  $kind = "body"
+  if ($outline -ge 1 -and $outline -le 6) {
+    $kind = "outline-heading"
+  } elseif ($text -match "^\d+(\.\d+)*\s+\S" -and $bold -ne 0) {
+    $kind = "numbered-heading"
+  } elseif ($fontName -like "*Consolas*" -or $fontNameAscii -like "*Consolas*" -or $text -match "^\s*\d+\s{2,}\S") {
+    $kind = "code"

+    $kind = "toc"

+    kind = $kind

+    style = $styleName
+    outlineLevel = $outline
+    fontName = $fontName
+    fontNameAscii = $fontNameAscii
+    fontSize = $fontSize
+    bold = $bold
+    italic = $italic
+    color = $color
+    shading = $shading
+    alignment = $alignment
+    leftIndent = $leftIndent
+    firstLineIndent = $firstIndent
+    lineSpacing = $lineSpacing
+    spaceBefore = $spaceBefore
+    spaceAfter = $spaceAfter
+  }
+}
+
+function Read-TableRecord {
+  param(
+    $Table,
+    [int]$Index
+  )
+
+  $cells = @()
+  $rowLimit = [Math]::Min([int]$Table.Rows.Count, 5)
+  $colLimit = [Math]::Min([int]$Table.Columns.Count, 5)
+
+  for ($row = 1; $row -le $rowLimit; $row++) {
+    for ($col = 1; $col -le $colLimit; $col++) {
+      $cellRange = $Table.Cell($row, $col).Range
+      $cells += [pscustomobject]@{
+        row = $row
+        col = $col
+        text = Normalize-Text $cellRange.Text
+        fontName = [string]$cellRange.Font.Name
+        fontNameAscii = [string]$cellRange.Font.NameAscii
+        fontSize = [double]$cellRange.Font.Size
+        bold = [int]$cellRange.Font.Bold
+        alignment = [string]$cellRange.ParagraphFormat.Alignment
+      }
+    }
+  }
+
+  [pscustomobject]@{
+    index = $Index
+    rows = [int]$Table.Rows.Count
+    cols = [int]$Table.Columns.Count
+    cells = $cells
+  }
+}
+
+$outputRootPath = Join-Path (Get-Location) $OutputRoot
+New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $outputRootPath | Out-Null
+
+$runPath = Join-Path $outputRootPath (Get-Date -Format "yyyyMMdd-HHmmss")
+New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $runPath | Out-Null
+
+$app = [System.Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal]::GetActiveObject("kwps.Application")
+$doc = $app.ActiveDocument
+if (-not $doc) {
+  throw "No active WPS document."
+}
+
+$paragraphs = @()
+$paragraphLimit = [Math]::Min([int]$doc.Paragraphs.Count, 160)
+for ($i = 1; $i -le $paragraphLimit; $i++) {
+  $paragraphs += Read-ParagraphRecord -Paragraph $doc.Paragraphs.Item($i) -Index $i
+}
+
+$tables = @()
+try {
+  for ($i = 1; $i -le $doc.Tables.Count; $i++) {
+    $tables += Read-TableRecord -Table $doc.Tables.Item($i) -Index $i
+  }
+} catch {}
+
+$tocText = @()
+$tocCount = 0
+try {
+  $tocCount = [int]$doc.TablesOfContents.Count
+  for ($i = 1; $i -le $tocCount; $i++) {

+  }
+} catch {}
+
+$fullText = [string]$doc.Content.Text
+$report = [pscustomobject]@{
+  document = [pscustomobject]@{
+    name = [string]$doc.Name
+    fullName = [string]$doc.FullName
+    paragraphCount = [int]$doc.Paragraphs.Count
+    tableCount = [int]$doc.Tables.Count
+    tocCount = $tocCount
+    textLength = $fullText.Length
+  }
+  tocText = $tocText
+  paragraphs = $paragraphs
+  tables = $tables
+}
+
+$jsonPath = Join-Path $runPath "wps-render-report.json"
+$report | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 8 | Set-Content -LiteralPath $jsonPath -Encoding UTF8
+
+$process = Get-Process -Name wps -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
+  Where-Object { $_.MainWindowHandle -ne 0 } |
+  Sort-Object StartTime -Descending |
+  Select-Object -First 1
+
+$shotPath = Join-Path $runPath "active-wps.png"
+if ($process) {
+  $captureScript = Join-Path (Get-Location) "scripts\capture-wps-window.ps1"
+  & $captureScript -ProcessId $process.Id -OutputPath $shotPath | Out-Null
+}
+
+Write-Output ("REPORT={0}" -f $jsonPath)
+Write-Output ("SCREENSHOT={0}" -f $shotPath)

<summary>Tool use: **apply_patch**</summary>
**Add: `d:\cursor_dev\wps_ai\scripts\capture-open-wps-section.ps1`**

```diff
+param(
+  [int]$ParagraphIndex = 1,
+  [string]$OutputPath = "test-artifacts\manual-inspect\wps-section.png"
+)
+
+$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
+
+$app = [System.Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal]::GetActiveObject("kwps.Application")
+$doc = $app.ActiveDocument
+if (-not $doc) {
+  throw "No active WPS document."
+}
+
+try { $app.Visible = $true } catch {}
+try { $app.WindowState = 1 } catch {}
+
+$process = Get-Process -Name wps -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
+  Where-Object { $_.MainWindowHandle -ne 0 -and $_.MainWindowTitle -like "*$($doc.Name)*" } |
+  Sort-Object StartTime -Descending |
+  Select-Object -First 1
+
+if (-not $process) {
+  $process = Get-Process -Name wps -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
+    Where-Object { $_.MainWindowHandle -ne 0 } |
+    Sort-Object StartTime -Descending |
+    Select-Object -First 1
+}
+
+Add-Type @"
+using System;
+using System.Runtime.InteropServices;
+public static class WpsSectionWindowTools {
+  [DllImport("user32.dll")]
+  public static extern bool SetForegroundWindow(IntPtr hWnd);
+  [DllImport("user32.dll")]
+  public static extern bool ShowWindow(IntPtr hWnd, int nCmdShow);
+}
+"@
+
+if ($process) {
+  [WpsSectionWindowTools]::ShowWindow($process.MainWindowHandle, 3) | Out-Null
+  [WpsSectionWindowTools]::SetForegroundWindow($process.MainWindowHandle) | Out-Null
+}
+
+$paragraphCount = [int]$doc.Paragraphs.Count
+$targetIndex = [Math]::Max(1, [Math]::Min($ParagraphIndex, $paragraphCount))
+$range = $doc.Paragraphs.Item($targetIndex).Range
+try { $range.Select() } catch {}
+try { $app.Selection.Range.Select() } catch {}
+try { $app.ScreenRefresh() } catch {}
+
+Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 900
+
+$fullOutputPath = Join-Path (Get-Location) $OutputPath
+$outputDir = Split-Path -Parent $fullOutputPath
+New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $outputDir | Out-Null
+
+$captureScript = Join-Path (Get-Location) "scripts\capture-wps-window.ps1"
+if (-not $process) {
+  throw "No visible WPS process."
+}
+
+& $captureScript -ProcessId $process.Id -OutputPath $fullOutputPath | Out-Null
+
+Write-Output ("SCREENSHOT={0}" -f $fullOutputPath)
```

function createHeadingMarker(state, level) {
  const normalizedLevel = Math.max(1, Math.min(6, Number(level) || 1));

  for (let index = 0; index < normalizedLevel - 1; index += 1) {
    if (!state.headingCounters[index]) {
      state.headingCounters[index] = 1;
    }
  }

  state.headingCounters[normalizedLevel - 1] =
    (state.headingCounters[normalizedLevel - 1] || 0) + 1;

  for (let index = normalizedLevel; index < state.headingCounters.length; index += 1) {
